title: Contract language + remedies for Dedicated throughput SLO (define terms, carve-outs, credits, references)
creator: Lauren Bishop
description:
Goal
Draft and align the Dedicated Throughput SLO contract/SLA clause set with Legal + SRE so Sales can use consistent language in Order Forms / MSAs.

Scope
- Definitions for Throughput SLO and related terms (Deployment, Dedicated Capacity, Tier, Burst, Throttling Event, Maintenance Window, Excluded Time)
- Measurement and reporting reference (explicit link-by-reference to the throughput measurement standard)
- Carve-outs/exclusions (customer-induced issues, invalid requests, exceeded quotas, incident maintenance, force majeure, etc.)
- Remedies/credits for sustained failure to meet the Throughput SLO (by tier)
- Clarify expected behavior under overload (admission control/backpressure vs “breach”)
- Exception path: higher-than-published guarantees / bespoke workloads / benchmark-based custom schedules

Out of scope
- Rewriting Redwood’s general uptime SLA
- Any contractual commitments on model output quality

Key stakeholders
- Legal: Michael Grant (sponsor), Sofia Mendes (commercial counsel)
- SRE: Rafael Mendes, Aisha Bello (SLO governance)
- Product: Lauren Bishop (DRI), Evelyn Hart (exec sponsor)
- GTM: Jordan Blake (exceptions + negotiation pressure)

References (drafts)
- Confluence: throughput measurement standard (architecture-and-standards/performance-standards/throughput-measurement-standard)
- Confluence: Dedicated Throughput SLO definition (eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/dedicated-throughput-slo-definition)
- Confluence: Dedicated tier definitions (product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/dedicated-tier-definitions)

Acceptance criteria
1) Legal-approved clause text for: definitions, measurement methodology reference, exclusions, and remedies.
2) Clear remedy structure (credits) that SRE agrees is measurable and enforceable.
3) Sales enablement has a “negotiation-safe” summary of what we can/can’t commit to (tie-in to cheat sheet).
4) Published location + owner for ongoing updates (so we don’t fork language in email threads).

Open questions (to resolve in this ticket)
- Do we define the SLO as a monthly objective (calendar month) or rolling window? Contract needs a clean objective period.
- Credits: percentage-of-monthly-fee vs fixed credit schedule; how to handle multi-deployment accounts.
- Can we cleanly exclude time spent in expected throttling (admission control) vs actual service degradation?
- How explicit should we be about required customer telemetry setup / request patterns to be eligible for remedies?

Proposed structure (strawman)
A) Definitions
B) Throughput SLO Objective (by tier)
C) Measurement methodology + reporting
D) Exclusions
E) Customer obligations (request validity, not exceeding agreed concurrency, notify us, cooperate)
F) Remedies / Service Credits
G) Exceptions / custom commitments

Notes
- Please keep language consistent with tier semantics: throttling may be the intended protective behavior and should not automatically trigger breach.
- Avoid committing to a single model’s exact tokens/sec unless explicitly in Order Form (tie back to tier definition assumptions + exclusions).
comments: 2025-01-29 (Lauren Bishop): Creating this as a launch-blocker. Sales is already asking for “copy/paste” language and we need to stop ad-hoc promises. Talia—can you run coordination with Sofia Mendes + SRE and land a final doc by next Wed?

2025-01-31 (Talia Benson): Kickoff scheduled w/ Sofia Mendes (Legal), Rafael + Aisha (SRE), Jordan (GTM) for Feb 4. Agenda: define objective period, carve-outs, and what’s an SLO miss vs expected throttling. I’ll circulate a first draft prior.

2025-02-04 (Talia Benson): Meeting notes: (1) Legal wants explicit reference-by-link to measurement standard doc; we should include version/date to avoid ambiguity. (2) SRE strongly prefers objective measured per calendar month (aligns to error budget tracking + reporting). (3) Key distinction: admission-control throttling = not an SLO breach, but we must describe it as ‘request limiting’ and ensure tier docs state burst expectations. Action: draft section separating ‘Throttling Events’ from ‘Throughput Degradation’ and align with ADR on burst policy.

2025-02-06 (Sofia Mendes): Please avoid terms like “guaranteed capacity” without the measurement conditions. Recommend: ‘Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to meet the Throughput SLO under the Measurement Standard, subject to exclusions.’ Also: remedies should be the sole and exclusive remedy for SLO failure; include standard limitation language. I can propose a credit table but need Finance to confirm ranges.

2025-02-07 (Laura Bennett): Finance preference: service credits as a % of the Dedicated monthly platform fee for the affected deployment(s), capped (e.g., 25%). Avoid unbounded credits tied to downstream customer revenue impact. If Sales needs higher credits for a strategic deal, route via exception path with pricing uplift.

2025-02-11 (Aisha Bello): From SLO governance: we can support credits if the SLI is computed the same way we alert internally (rate over 5-min windows, aggregated over the month, excluding maintenance + customer errors). We cannot support credits based on customer-side measurements unless they align exactly to our exported metrics. Suggest contract language: Redwood’s metrics are the source of truth.

2025-02-14 (Talia Benson): Draft v1 shared with Legal/SRE (internal doc: dedicated-throughput-slo-contract-language). Open items: wording for ‘eligible requests’ and whether to exclude ‘customer-selected max_tokens too high’ scenarios. SRE leaning to exclude only malformed/invalid and explicit overload beyond agreed concurrency ceiling; otherwise it becomes too subjective.

2025-02-19 (Jordan Blake): Flagging prospect negotiation pressure (Helio + Northpeak): they want ‘no throttling’ language. We should be clear: Premium tier minimizes throttling under stated burst policy, but we won’t contractually promise zero throttling. Request: add a one-paragraph plain-English explanation Sales can paste into redlines.

2025-02-21 (Michael Grant): Legal review: overall OK direction. Must tighten exclusions (Force majeure + customer network/VPC issues for Private networking components if applicable) and ensure consistency with existing Master Terms. Please add a clause that Scheduled Maintenance is excluded and define notice requirements (e.g., 72 hours, except emergency).

2025-02-26 (Talia Benson): Updated draft v2: added (1) Scheduled Maintenance definition + notice policy, (2) explicit ‘Redwood metrics are authoritative’ sentence, (3) credit schedule proposal: if monthly Throughput SLO attainment < 99% then 5% credit; < 97% then 10%; < 95% then 20%; cap 25%. Still needs Finance signoff on thresholds and Legal wording. Also added Sales-friendly paragraph on throttling vs breach.

2025-03-03 (Sofia Mendes): v2 is close. Remaining edits: replace ‘attainment < 99%’ phrasing with ‘Failure to meet Throughput SLO during the Objective Period’ and define calculation in appendix referencing the measurement standard. Also ensure customers must submit a written claim within 30 days of the month end and that credits require account to be in good standing. Marking as ready for final review once Finance confirms table.
